construct: Transthyretin amyloidosis results from destabilization of transthyretin tetramers and extracellular deposition of misfolded transthyretin fibrils; myocardial infiltration increases ventricular wall thickness and stiffness and produces a restrictive cardiomyopathy.

blueprint.competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: An older patient with HFpEF, bilateral carpal tunnel history, increased wall thickness with relatively low voltage, no monoclonal protein, and grade-3 Tc-PYP myocardial uptake has ATTR cardiac amyloidosis.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: AL amyloidosis is not the best answer after a negative monoclonal-protein evaluation combined with strong grade 2/3 bone-tracer uptake. HCM, hypertension, and hemochromatosis do not reproduce the ATTR scintigraphy pattern.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Because the stem explicitly supplies both the exclusion of a monoclonal process and grade-3 PYP uptake, the common AL-versus-ATTR ambiguity is intentionally removed.
